title: Personal space and permission
subject: RSHE

thread_tags.line: Thread tags: SMSC S/M/So (C: none); British Values IL/MR (D/RL/T: none).
thread_tags.rationale: S: consider a fictional person’s dignity and choices. M: distinguish respectful actions from pressure or intrusion. So: listen and respond to another person’s boundary. IL: respect a choice to pause or use an aid. MR: respect privacy, personal space and a refusal. No other thread is claimed.

label: Public edition
objective_verbatim: Ask permission for an everyday action and respect another person’s response.
display_objective: Show how a teen can ask first and respect a reply.
approved_activity: Use fictional cards about borrowing an item, sitting nearby or offering help to practise asking first.
Choose a response when someone says no, seems unsure or changes their mind; rehearse with an adult if preferred.
calendar_note: Year A. 23–27 November 2026. One 40-minute lesson. No day or clock slot inferred. Week 7 is assessing.
where_this_leads: This helps me respect other people’s space, belongings and choices.
unit: Body privacy, personal space and permission
accreditation: The qualification and the accredited unit: staff confirm any mapping from actual work. No criteria or completion are inferred.
assessment: Weeks 1–6 are formative. Week 7 is the assessing lesson. Keep actual responses, support, gaps and next steps in the evidence record.

sources.note: The owner-approved standalone RSHE outline is the weekly teaching source. The three build notes apply throughout. No separate workbook row is asserted.

authoring_provenance.note: Newly authored tasks from the owner-approved RSHE outline. No separate workbook row is asserted. All people and situations are fictional. Accurate anatomical terms and everyday permission principles were checked against primary guidance.

external_sources.note: Approval, curriculum context, template and authored visual provenance.

evidence.description: A permission request and responses to two boundary situations, recorded in the learner’s chosen mode.
evidence.status: not prefilled; actual response and support to be recorded

routes.Supported: Supported: choose a relevant permission request from two choices, then choose respectful actions for two different boundary stories, with reading or scribing support.
routes.Independent: Independent: compose a request for borrowing, sitting nearby or offering help, then record responses and reasons for two different boundary situations.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: retain the request and two responses, explain an unclear reply and a changed mind, and show how the person can avoid pressure.

vocab.definition: A freely given yes to a clear request.
Use a question to find something out.
An answer in words, signs or an aid.
Not yet sure about a choice.
An option a person can pick.

cases.text: A young person wants to borrow a pen for a task. The owner says no.
cases.next_step: A request could be: could the young person use the pen for this task? After no, leave it and find another pen. Do not demand a reason or keep pressing.

cases.text: A young person asks to sit nearby. The other person says they are not sure.
cases.next_step: Do not move closer. Offer time and another seat. The person does not need to explain a private reason.

cases.text: A young person agrees to have help with a model. Then they ask for the help to stop.
cases.next_step: Respect the changed mind. Do not carry on because the first answer was yes.

cases.text: A young person offers help with a bag. There is no clear reply.
cases.judgement: Wait and check. Do not take the bag.
cases.next_step: No clear reply is not agreement. Allow time and a usual communication aid. Do not infer consent from a smile or a photograph.

cases.text: A young person asks to borrow a pen for one task. The owner freely points to yes on their aid.
cases.judgement: The agreed use can go ahead.
cases.next_step: Use the pen only for that task and return it. Check again for a different use. A clear response can be non-speaking.

cases.text: A young person says no to lending an item. The other person keeps asking for a yes.
cases.next_step: Respect the first refusal. Repeated requests used to wear someone down are not respectful permission seeking.

We Do: 5 minutes.
Teacher: A respects an unclear response. Silence, uncertainty or lack of a spoken no is not agreement. A clear freely given yes may be spoken, signed, pointed to or communicated through an aid; speech and eye contact are not required. If someone changes their mind, stop the action. Reteach with the unsure-seat card, keeping the exchange fictional and avoiding repeated pressure.

pupil_text: Words that help
Permission: A freely given yes to a clear request.
Space: Room around a person.
Ask: Use a question to find something out.
Reply: An answer in words, signs or an aid.
Unsure: Not yet sure about a choice.
Stop: End the action now.
Choice: An option a person can pick.
